stories.headline: Liberal Party leadership crisis as Taylor emerges as challenger to Ley after Hastie withdraws
stories.summary: A prolonged Liberal Party leadership crisis intensified as Andrew Hastie withdrew from challenging Sussan Ley, clearing the path for Angus Taylor. Secret meetings between conservative MPs failed to resolve who should challenge Ley, while the Coalition split with the Nationals prompted Ley to appoint an interim Liberal-only shadow cabinet.

stories.headline: RBA expected to raise interest rates in February as inflation exceeds forecasts
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is widely expected to raise the cash rate to 3.85% at its February meeting after inflation data came in above expectations. All major banks now predict a rate hike, which would be the first increase in over two years and represent an embarrassing U-turn after three rate cuts in 2025.

stories.headline: Albanese navigates various political challenges from Israeli President visit to Trump diplomacy
stories.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese addressed multiple political situations including urging restraint from protesters during Israeli President Isaac Herzog's upcoming visit to Australia, dodging questions about Trump's 'Board of Peace' offer, and facing criticism over government spending contributing to inflation. Commentary focused on his 'politics of kindness' approach and Labor's strong electoral position.

stories.headline: Kinetic IT wins ADF base services contact centre support contract
stories.summary: Australian technology services provider Kinetic IT secured an ICT contract with the Australian Department of Defence to support its base services contact centre. The centre is part of the ADF's Base Services Transformation Program and serves as the primary contact point for all base services across the Defence estate.

articles.title: Kinetic IT secures support contract for ADF's base services contact centre

stories.headline: NSW Greens to introduce bill expanding council powers over berry farming
stories.summary: NSW Greens member Cate Faehrmann will move a private member's bill to give councils more regulatory power over blueberry and berry farms, which she says currently benefit from a 'massive carve-out' from planning laws. The move responds to resident concerns about environmental hazards and land devaluation from the rapidly expanding berry industry.

articles.title: NSW Greens to move bill to let councils better regulate berry industry as it continues rapid expansion
